content.title: About
content.content: Plantains are large tropical berries of the banana family that are usually eaten when ripe. Unlike bananas, they are typically cooked before consumption—boiled, fried, or baked. A ripe raw plantain has a mildly sweet flavor, creamy texture, and provides a range of beneficial nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plantains are often called “cooking bananas” because they are used in prepared dishes rather than eaten fresh.
They have many regional names: in Africa they are called “plantain,” in the Caribbean “plantain,” and in Southeast Asia “pisang kepok.”
Several varieties exist, differing in size, skin color, and sweetness level.
Plantains are a staple source of carbohydrates in many African and Latin American diets.
The peel contains starch that converts to sugars as the fruit ripens, making it sweeter over time.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides a steady source of energy and promotes lasting satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and supports the immune system.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Plantains contain thiamine, riboflavin, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestive health and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: The high starch content can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to banana family plants.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ripe raw plantains can be sliced and added to salads, smoothies, or desserts. They are most often prepared by boiling, frying, baking, or mashing. Before cooking, the skin is usually peeled, which becomes soft as the fruit ripens.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep plantains at room temperature until they ripen. Once ripe, store them in the refrigerator for up to 3‑5 days. Avoid airtight bags, which can accelerate ripening and cause mold growth.
